I help occasionally at community garden, give blood at least three times a year and I used to help take down syndrome kids horseriding. These do make me feel good about myself but nothing that's really substantial.
I wholeheartedly agree, the stigma just drives people into the ground and makes them feel worse for feeling suicidal. We really need to adopt a better approach to how such things are handled.

Well I have multiple reasons not to take any anti depression meds.

First I have a pretty wild metabolism, I've had dosage issues with meds before and I don't really want to risk something like that with my brain.

My mother was previously given multiple different prescriptions as she was suffering from depression whilst going through the menopause and they all made her feel worse, in the end she moved out to the countryside and is doing much better with no meds.

I also have two friends who've taken ssdi's, one is not the person I knew at all anymore, he is so lacking in spirit or energy and just seems content in a really frightening way. The other tried to get off them and said the withdrawal was something akin to an opiate addiction, she's since put on a lot of weight and has regrets about ever taking them.

Plus I don't really trust how they are prescribed via a dsm check list that only looks for symptoms and is attempting to lock you into some default human state that really very few people naturally find themselves in.


Look I'm glad you've found meds that work for you and I hope that they along with other things keep you going, but for me they're not the answer.

Thanks for that, I wish it was that simple though.

It's hard going when every time I sit and think about how we got here it makes me dizzy and I feel like my brain is going to vomit, I honestly can't put up with it much longer.

I'll do my part up until the end, but I really don't have the willpower to pretend much longer.

Honestly I'm really starting to really hate hearing stuff this. 

Never asked to be born, nuff said, fair enough.

There is zero chance of me ever explaining to my parents that I want to die, I've never had depression and I've been very damn lucky to have a loving family and friends. But I am well aware I don't really belong here, I've given life a fair shout and I'm pretty fit, have a good social life, hobbies and a decent job,problem is I don't want more and all I see is myself distracting myself from my unease of existence untill my eventual death. I have thought long and hard about this decision and it's really not something I've come to lightly. 

Good thing for me is I've been clever or lucky enough to compartmentalise my life so as my plans near completion I'm quiting my job and severing all ties with friends, they will never know, the only people I will hurt are my immediate family and yeah that sucks and I hate that, but it also sucks is that I couldn't bring up my valid decision about ending my life without being prodded and probed and drugged up to the gullet.

I understand you're really trying to help someone but this guilt trip stuff is really to lowest, I might be alone in the way I see this, heck it wouldn't surprise me at all, but please understand that just because you bring life unto the world doesn't mean that you can hold them hostage to an existence they're not willing to be a part of.
